description: CC adapter (reference) vs RINO's local execution backend (candidate). Covers the RINO P6 v0 conformance producer (rino-ahp-conformance) gate-replies dry-run and keeps the RINO P2 first-cut staging entries that production RINO still needs; the P2 entries are expected to be unused when the candidate is the P6 conformance producer. Every entry says why the difference is intended; anything not listed fails the diff.

allow.reason: P6 v0, RINO conformance vs CC: both sides write decisions into the gate envelope and publish the same list in capabilities.json (tool.pre allow/ask/deny, permission.request allow/deny, input.request accept/decline, turn.stop ack/block; no D12 divergence). The CC adapter unlinks a finished gate's pending/<seq>-<event>.json once the decision is taken (commit cd292a2; conformance G07/E07 derive gates from events.jsonl for this reason), so shadow_diff reads the reference notice as '<absent>' while rino-ahp-conformance keeps it. Spec 5.1 makes decisions SHOULD on gate events, so no decision is missing.

P6 v0 retention difference: default_decision is identical in both capabilities.json (tool.pre deny, permission.request deny, input.request decline, turn.stop ack) and follows the fail-closed defaults in spec 9.2/9.3. CC deletes the finished pending notice (cd292a2) so shadow_diff sees '<absent>'; rino-ahp-conformance keeps the notice. Spec 5.1 makes default_decision SHOULD on gate events.

gate.pending is synthesized by shadow_diff from whether a pending notice is still on disk. CC deletes pending/<seq>-<event>.json after reply/timeout (cd292a2; 'pending' lists only unresolved requests, and conformance G07/E07 were updated), while rino-ahp-conformance keeps it as an audit artifact. Both wrote the notice while the gate was open and both wrote the ack; intended housekeeping difference, not a gate that stayed blocked.

P6 v0: the CC pending envelope carried timeout_ms (the gate-replies scenario deliberately sets 1500 ms), but the finished notice is unlinked (cd292a2) so shadow_diff sees '<absent>'; rino-ahp-conformance retains the notice with 1500 ms. Both capabilities.json declare the same 1500 ms (no D12 divergence), so the actual gate timeout agrees. Spec 5.1 makes timeout_ms SHOULD on gate events; 1500 is scenario config, not the 120000 default.

P6 v0, RINO conformance vs CC: rule content is not standardized (spec 11). CC's default rules.json adds the host-specific agent-artifact-dirs rule (CC agent-runtime artifact directories) to the four built-ins the spec recommends; rino-ahp-conformance ships exactly those four shared rules and marks them all applied. Pinning cand makes a dropped or renamed shared rule fail; rules.required is empty on both sides and rules.sha256 is covered by rino-rules-file.

Same CC-only default rule: CC reports agent-artifact-dirs as applied because it ships it; RINO P6 v0 does not implement that host-specific rule and therefore must not publish a status for it (spec 11: every shipped rule gets a status). Statuses for the four shared rules match.

RINO P2 v1 declares only tool.pre and turn.stop as gates; permission.request / input.request come after interrupt->resume is wired (spec Appendix B, staged declaration). Spec 4.2: MUST NOT list them until then. The P6 v0 rino-ahp-conformance producer already declares both gates, so this entry is unused in the gate-replies dry-run; it stays for the production-RINO P2 comparison.

Same staging: in headless cli, RINO's ApprovalGate Ask is a deny and the tool.pre gate is the only consumer decision point. The P6 v0 conformance producer emits both events, so this entry is unused in the gate-replies dry-run; remove it when production RINO declares the gates.

RINO has no subagents, worktrees, teammates, slash expansion, mid-run model switch or CC-style config/file hooks (P0 mapping 1, 1.1). Spec 4.1: undeclared events are not emitted. P6 v0 rino-ahp-conformance declares these events too, so this entry is unused against it; it stays for production RINO P2.
In-process producer: no host hook timeout, so its own ceiling (RINO plans 600000) applies instead of CC's 180s-10s (spec 9.2).

RINO P2 first cut declares updated_input=false until its rule engine re-runs rules on rewritten input (P0 mapping Q5). P6 v0 rino-ahp-conformance declares updated_input=true (same as CC), so this entry is unused against it; it stays for production RINO P2.

additional_context needs the adk TurnPreparer seam (decision-adk-fragment-seam, phase 3). P6 v0 rino-ahp-conformance declares additional_context=true, so this entry is unused against it; it stays for production RINO P2.

consumer.json may ask turn.stop for up to 300000; CC clamps to 170000, production RINO can honour it (spec 9.2). Unused in the P6 v0 gate-replies dry-run: CC deletes the finished pending notice, so the event-level reference value is '<absent>' (covered by rino-p6-gate-timeout-retained), and both capabilities declare the scenario timeout.

CC reports partially_applied when it clamps turn.stop or cannot gate an async hook; RINO may apply the same consumer.json fully. The gate-replies scenario writes no consumer.json and both sides declare 'absent', so this entry is unused there; it stays for scenarios/production where CC clamps.

RINO ships its own rules file in the same schema (tool_kinds instead of CC tool names), so the digest differs (P0 mapping Q9). Rule ids and status are compared except for the CC-only agent-artifact-dirs rule (rino-p6-no-agent-artifact-dirs-ids / -status); required is still compared.
